notes: Representative human-reviewed changes highlighted by NIST for CSF 2.0: an explicit all-sector scope, the new GOVERN function, and stronger governance and supply-chain emphasis. Each quote is unique on its recorded side after whitespace collapsing and absent from the opposite side.

changes.old_quote: While this document was developed to improve cybersecurity risk management in critical infrastructure, the Framework can be used by organizations in any sector or community.
changes.new_quote: The Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 is designed to help organizations of all sizes and sectors — including industry, government, academia, and nonprofit — to manage and reduce their cybersecurity risks.
changes.note: CSF 2.0 foregrounds its applicability to organizations of all sizes and sectors.

changes.old_quote: The Framework Core consists of five concurrent and continuous Functions—Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover.
changes.new_quote: The CSF Core Functions — GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, and RECOVER — organize cybersecurity outcomes at their highest level.
changes.note: The Core adds GOVERN to the five existing Functions.

changes.new_quote: Building on previous versions, CSF 2.0 contains new features that highlight the importance of governance and supply chains.
changes.note: CSF 2.0 explicitly highlights governance and supply-chain risk.
